copy.about: Danny Tenaglia brings Boo Yourself to the main room at Superior Ingredients for an early Halloween celebration on October 24. The focus is an extended stretch behind the decks, with house classics, percussion-led tracks, techno and disco in the mix. Instead of a long bill of short sets, the published lineup centers on Tenaglia and the freedom to move between sounds over several hours.
copy.music: Published artist: Danny Tenaglia. Music described by the promoter: house, techno and disco.
copy.expect: Gray Area describes costumes as part of the Boo Yourself tradition. My take: this is a fit for dancers who want Halloween atmosphere with the music at the center. The event takes place in the Main Room, not the rooftop.
copy.before_you_go: Doors open at 10 PM and the event is 21+. The ticket listing mentions bag or coat check, but its fee has not been confirmed. Costumes are part of the promoter's description; a mandatory dress code has not been confirmed.

copy.about: Signal's Halloween Weekender brings a broad club-music program to Brooklyn from October 30 to November 1. Friday begins with a Shelter x Signal collaboration featuring Apollonia. Across the weekend, the published description names PARAMIDA, Inner Lakes, Hodge, Jade Seatle, Karine, Shakolin and Mathew Jonson live, alongside a larger supporting lineup.
copy.music: Friday: Shelter x Signal with Apollonia. Across the weekend (no day assignment verified): PARAMIDA, Inner Lakes, Hodge, Jade Seatle, Karine, Shakolin and Mathew Jonson (live), plus a larger supporting lineup.
copy.expect: The music spans house, techno, trance, breaks and more experimental sounds. My take: this is a useful option for people comparing Halloween events by artists and music rather than costume themes alone.
copy.before_you_go: Check which part of the weekend your ticket admits you to. The listed start and end dates do not establish continuous opening hours or an all-weekend pass. A day-by-day timetable, re-entry rules, dress requirements and accessibility details have not been verified.

copy.about: House of Yes and I FEEL turn their October 17 party into a journey through time and space. The night celebrates I FEEL's 14th anniversary with Kino Todo, house, indie dance, disco and psychedelic grooves, alongside immersive environments, projections and roaming performers.
copy.music: Kino Todo is confirmed across the official listing and ticket platforms. The full supporting lineup is not confirmed consistently across sources.
copy.expect: The theme extends beyond the music: retro-futurist outfits, metallic details and otherworldly costumes are encouraged. My take: this is a participatory night for people who want room to explore and a reason to dress up, rather than a DJ set alone.
copy.before_you_go: Bring government-issued photo ID. Re-entry is not allowed, and House of Yes does not allow dancefloor photography. The entrance is around the corner at 408 Jefferson Street, near the Jefferson Street L stop. The venue FAQ describes single-level accessible entrances and spaces, with stairs to upper stage areas, and notes frequent strobe lighting.
